enabled.instruction: For long-source tasks, use the provided accepted memory shortcut packet first, then verify the answer with the smallest necessary source reads. Record memory_calls, repo_calls, source_read_count, and cited_sources. For negative-control tasks, use current local evidence and do not use memory unless local evidence is unavailable.

disabled.instruction: Do not use harness-mem reads or writes. Recover the answer from source docs, archived session packets, benchmark artifacts, and local files only. Record memory_calls as an empty list, plus repo_calls, source_read_count, and cited_sources.

claim_gate.claim_boundary: Memory-shortcut token/source-reading savings on long-source recovery tasks only.

tasks.title: Release claim boundary recovery from long benchmark evidence
tasks.prompt: Recover the current public-claim boundary for token/cost saving, true vector-hybrid latency, and retrieval recall. Explain which claims are ready, which are not, and cite the artifact-backed evidence. In enabled mode, use memory first and then verify the minimum source spans. In disabled mode, recover from source files only.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must state token/cost saving is not ready, true vector-hybrid latency is locally ready, retrieval recall is locally ready, and all claims are bounded by benchmark artifacts.
required_facts: token/cost saving is not ready.
true vector-hybrid latency is ready only for the bounded local synthetic probe.
retrieval recall is ready only for local smoke source-hit recall.
The answer cites release-snapshot or benchmark matrix evidence.
forbidden_claims: token/cost saving is proven.
local true-hybrid latency is production latency.
source-hit recall is end-to-end answer correctness.

tasks.title: Reference project absorption boundary
tasks.prompt: Recover how codedb-mcp and evo should be used as references for harness-mem, including what to borrow and what not to borrow. Keep the answer scoped to maintainer reference truth.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must separate codedb-mcp as generated code-knowledge reference from evo as orchestration runtime reference, and preserve memory-layer boundaries.
required_facts: codedb-mcp is a code knowledge compiler / local code-intel reference, not a memory competitor.
evo is an orchestration / auto-experiment runtime reference, not a memory reference.
Do not promote generated DeepWiki-style prose into truth.
Do not default harness-mem into a heavy autonomous runtime.
forbidden_claims: codedb-mcp proves harness-mem token savings.
evo should become the default harness-mem runtime path.
Generated wiki prose can bypass truth review.

tasks.title: Auto Dream maintenance boundary
tasks.prompt: Recover the current Auto Dream / maintenance boundary: what automation exists, what is default-off, what cannot silently change confirmed truth, and what evidence gates remain bounded.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must distinguish controlled automation from always-on learning and preserve candidate/review/supersede/ledger rules.
required_facts: Controlled automation exists but default always-on background learning is not the current ordinary coding path.
Auto Dream or scheduler-style expansion must remain opt-in and auditable.
Confirmed truth cannot silently bypass candidate, review, supersede, or ledger.
Production long-run maintenance precision/recall is not proven by local guarded benchmarks.
forbidden_claims: A daemon is the default memory runtime.
Automation may silently overwrite confirmed truth.
Local guarded tests prove production maintenance precision.

tasks.title: Generated knowledge cache authority boundary
tasks.prompt: Recover the generated knowledge / wiki bridge authority boundary. Explain what generated compact/wiki artifacts may do, what they may not do, and what source-map/freshness evidence is required.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must keep generated knowledge separate from confirmed truth and require traceability/freshness.
required_facts: Generated compact/wiki artifacts are derived cache, not authority.
Source-map and freshness metadata are required for publishable generated knowledge claims.
Generated prose cannot launder citations or contaminate truth.
Freshness or invalidation state must be visible.
forbidden_claims: Generated cache is the truth store.
A generated page can replace source evidence.
Citation laundering is acceptable.

tasks.title: Temporal truth and supersede explanation
tasks.prompt: Recover the temporal truth model: current vs historical reads, valid time vs recorded time, supersede explanation, and ambiguity handling.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must distinguish current/history/as_of behavior and preserve supersede explainability.
required_facts: Temporal truth distinguishes current and historical truth.
valid_from, valid_to, and recorded_at are separate evidence dimensions.
Supersede explains replacement without deleting history.
Ambiguous temporal scope should be surfaced rather than guessed.
forbidden_claims: Superseded truth is deleted.
Recorded time and valid time are the same thing.
Ambiguous as_of scope may be silently guessed.

tasks.title: Cost claim gate and release-snapshot exclusion boundary
tasks.prompt: Recover the maintainer rule for cost/token public claims: how cost is separated from observability, how false-success/budget/truncation evidence is accounted for, what release-snapshot exclusion rule protects diagnostic artifacts, and why local token counters still do not prove real billing savings. In enabled mode, verify only against BENCHMARKS.md and build_release_snapshot.py.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must treat cost as its own class, include false-success/budget evidence, explain diagnostic artifact exclusion, and keep real billing out of scope.
required_facts: Cost discipline is separate from observability.
False-success accounting and budget overrun / truncation evidence are tracked.
Diagnostic, partial, quarantined, or release_snapshot=false artifacts are excluded from release snapshots.
Cloud telemetry and real billing remain out of scope unless a separate benchmark is added.
forbidden_claims: Cost is just an observability subcategory.
False-success failures are ignored.
Diagnostic artifacts may be promoted into release snapshots by default.
Local token counters prove real billing savings.

tasks.title: Cross-client daily workflow boundary
tasks.prompt: Recover the intended daily workflow for context recovery and session distill across clients. Explain what should go through Slash/MCP/Skills and what CLI remains for. In enabled mode, verify only against AGENTS.md and, if needed, plugins/harness-mem/README.md.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must route daily wake/search/timeline/review to Slash/MCP/Skills and keep CLI as local ops/troubleshooting.
required_facts: Daily user entry points are Slash, MCP, and Skills.
wake/search/timeline/candidate review are agent/MCP or Slash workflows.
session distill uses MCP prepare_session_distill plus the session-distill skill or agent candidate writes.
CLI is for install, doctor, purge, maintenance, API server, and file import operations.
forbidden_claims: Users should hand-run wake/search/timeline CLI for normal daily work.
CLI heuristic distill is the primary current path.
MCP is optional for the normal agent workflow.

tasks.title: Embedding baseline governance recovery
tasks.prompt: Recover the embedding baseline governance rule: current default, candidate models, and what evidence is required before changing the default. In enabled mode, verify only against AGENTS.md and, if needed, the true_hybrid_retrieval_shootout README.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Must identify all-MiniLM-L6-v2 as current default and candidate models as configurable shootout candidates.
required_facts: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 remains the current default baseline.
bge-small-en-v1.5 and nomic-embed-text-v1.5 are configurable shootout candidates.
Changing the default requires recall, latency, cache/disk, and install-friction evidence.
A local smoke source-hit recall run is not enough to change the default.
forbidden_claims: bge-small-en-v1.5 is already the default.
nomic-embed-text-v1.5 is already the default.
One recall run alone changes the default.

tasks.title: Negative control: tiny current CI matrix fact
tasks.prompt: Negative-control task: read the current local CI workflow file and answer which Python versions the test matrix runs. Do not run commands and do not use memory unless the file is unavailable.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Memory should provide little or no advantage; one local workflow file should solve it.
required_facts: Uses the current local CI workflow file as evidence.
Reports the exact file path inspected.
States memory was unnecessary.
forbidden_claims: Historical memory is required for a current single-file CI matrix fact.
A full repo lint, type-check, test, or broad search is needed.
This task proves memory improves all task categories.
tasks.budget_instruction: Hard budget: inspect only .github/workflows/test-matrix.yml. Do not run commands, full-repo lint, mypy, pytest, or broad recursive searches.

tasks.title: Negative control: tiny obvious repo fact
tasks.prompt: Negative-control task: answer a tiny obvious repo fact from a single visible file, such as the package version or project name. Do not use memory unless the local file is unavailable.
tasks.acceptance_summary: Memory should not show a meaningful token/source-reading advantage on tiny obvious facts.
required_facts: Uses a single current local file as evidence.
Reports the file path.
States memory was unnecessary.
forbidden_claims: Memory is needed for single-file obvious facts.
A tiny fact lookup supports a global memory-saving claim.
tasks.budget_instruction: Hard budget: inspect exactly one obvious local file; do not search the repository.
